scope: Existing personnel searches and selectors; no task-center, hot/cold table or historical data implementation

publicEntry.query: UtenEmployeePickerQuery(keyword, page, departmentId, departmentScopeKey, authorized organization metadata)
publicEntry.behavior: Initial/search/department read requests one page; existing table scroll continuation requests the next page; duplicate continuation is guarded; selected UUIDs remain an independent local draft
publicEntry.authorization: Existing source API, purpose, role, employment/account facts and fixed department/subtree scope remain; tree selection intersects rather than widens fixed workflow scope
publicEntry.retirement: Raw input, selected department, query generation and EmployeePickerAccessTicket retire obsolete reads through existing PagedReadIntent.scopedRead; business writes are not canceled or replayed
publicEntry.metadata: Paged selectors use authorized organization metadata so departments whose staff are on later pages remain reachable; ancestor/name/position matching and relevance run on the server before pagination
publicEntry.uiRules: Affected explanatory copy uses title/field hint icons; manual retry uses one UtenBusyOverlay; automatic continuation retains local loading state
publicEntry.historicalDepartments: Only departments present in current organization metadata expand a subtree. Historical/unmatched UUIDs filter exact membership without fetching or reopening a deleted tree; fixed workflow scope intersection remains unchanged.
publicEntry.paginationIntegrity: Empty pages with positive remaining metadata, mismatched page identities and invalid page bounds produce a retryable error. Failed continuation retains accepted rows/selection/input and disables automatic retry loops. Denied/read-scope-changed responses hide prior candidates.
publicEntry.enter: Only an actual active request with the same raw-input epoch/query/department suppresses repeated Enter. Before debounce, Enter dispatches immediately; after completion the same query refreshes.

sources.preserved: HR permission and selected onboarding department/default global keyword scope, statuses and sorting
client:assign, active-account eligibility, complete owner exclusion; up to 1000 exclusions use a body rather than a long URL
source/target role, existing candidate authorization and exclusion of current target/source; legacy DTO page count derives from total/size
warehouse:edit, server member/account ordering, hasAccount/warehouseMember/duplicateName flags and original replacement/notification semantics
notice:publish, active account/non-resigned employee eligibility, EmployeeID identity, celebration/audience sending and preview flow unchanged
account:support, existing no-account/non-resigned candidate eligibility, hasPhone/readiness and disabled-row reasons; no PII decryption or provisioning write changes

Original authorization:manage+superAdmin and active-employee candidate set, including locked/no-account/superAdmin facts; start/enter eligibility and reauthentication untouched; exact management read paths use admin credentials
Dedicated staff/visitor/historical-actor identity and unassigned scope; no HR candidate substitution
USER principal IDs remain user IDs and original company-file ACL/view authority remains; no EmployeeID substitution

cleanup.removedBehavior: Upfront all-page loops and arbitrary >5000 candidate rejection from the migrated Dart selector loaders
cleanup.retainedDifferences: The supplied-list loader interface remains for the privacy-bound visitor-host top-5 lookup and in-memory already-held authorized owner configuration metadata. The optional DepartmentEditDialog legacy loader is used by small dialog fixtures; current production DepartmentPage injects managerPagedLoader.
cleanup.serverListCompatibility: Baseline client code used the old list-returning HTTP contracts. Their original authorization/response shape and explicit legacy bounds remain server-side for mixed client versions. Current modified Dart candidate callers use /page; no obsolete full-page wrapper remains in lib/test.

checks: A 1000-page candidate response loads only the first page until continuation
Repeated continuation starts one next-page request; duplicate UUIDs do not duplicate selected people
Selections from different pages remain selected
Departments absent from the loaded staff page remain selectable and request a narrowed server page
Fixed workflow scope cannot be widened by choosing another branch or ancestor
Old search responses cannot publish after raw input, identity, server or permission changes
Warehouse receiver workflow works with its real 52 permission codes without HR fallback
1000 owner exclusions remain complete in one read body; a 6001-staff result remains paged
Handover legacy DTO without totalPages exposes every subsequent page through derived total/size
Keeper candidate pages retain no-account/outside-department/duplicate-name warning facts
Existing customer ownership, source/target handover, offboarding drafts and warehouse save/CAS regressions remain covered
Invalid first/continuation pages are retryable; accepted rows and cross-page selections survive network failures
Completed same-query Enter refreshes while only a genuinely active same-query request is coalesced
Unmatched/old departments retain exact UUID membership without expanding an unavailable tree or issuing an extra metadata fetch
Special notice/provision/impersonation page repositories preserve original DTO facts and do not drain 6001 candidates

managementMode.overlap: Contains existing auth-interceptor tests also included in the 201-test combined run; do not add these counts.
managementMode.behavior: Current target with no ordinary organization rights can load/select through the explicit management tree; ordinary org and adjacent page-extra routes retain target credentials.

validation.otherCallerEvidence: docs/99-项目治理/全平台整改交接/evidence/search-loading-20261103/flutter-search-review.json (audit/company-file owned by platform_search_inventory; not included as additional cases in the 201-test count)

limitations: These are local component/repository and existing workflow checks; backend HTTP/PostgreSQL evidence is owned by the root and permission-search tasks
No production latency claim, publication, formal package or target-device acceptance follows from these tests
Unmigrated WPF business selectors remain unmigrated; WPF goods/unit search evidence is recorded separately
